title: T311-900SD DEBRIS ENVIRONMENT MODELLING IN CIS-LUNAR SPACE (EXPRO+)
description: Description:  Currently, debris environment models for cislunar space are very limited as such have been primarily developed for Earth-bound orbits. Such models are a necessary asset for collision/impact risk assessment and traffic coordination. With the expansion of human activities beyond Earth, notably in cislunar space, there is an increasing need for models and tools to support missions. This need is reflected on the latest Space Debris Mitigation requirements for lunar orbits, including disposal and availability of space traffic coordination methods. With various studies having explored disposed objects and debris clouds in cislunar space, the development of such models becomes increasingly feasible. Methods and software tools to perform assessments in Earth orbits exist and are well-used. To ensure safe operations and sustainability in cislunar space, an extended density-based model can be used for risk event statistics, delta-v planning for collision avoidance manoeuvres and reliability assessment due to impacts. The model shall leverage the results of recent studies on debris and clouds around the Moon and build upon the well-established tools andmethodologies for Earth orbits. For the dynamically complex lunar orbits, a long-term propagator is needed to support the characterisation and evolution of the population.   Under this activity, cislunar long-term propagators are aimed to be coupled with break-up, lunar impact, and traffic models to create a consistent debris and dust density map for the cislunar environment. To demonstrate the usability and mission application, the model shall be coupled with collision and impact risk assessment tool and tested on a Lunar mission design.

title: ESA SPACE WEATHER SERVICE NETWORK PRE-OPERATION, EVOLUTIONARY MAINTENANCE AND DEVELOPMENT
description: The present activity pursues two main objectives.First, it shall ensure the continued high-quality provision of pre-operational space weather services under the existing SWE Service Network. This includes maintaining the availability of the products and servicescurrently included in the Network portfolio through the SWE Service Portal, ensuring the integration of newly developed or updated products, providing first- and second-line end-user support, delivering tailored bulletins to high-priority users, and performing continuous and evolutionary maintenance of key service components.In addition, the service catalogue shall be updated and adapted to reflect emerging and future needs of a European operational space weather service.Second, the activity shall define, design, and implement a modern Research-to-Operations-to-Research (R2O2R) framework for space weather products and services. This shall include the analysis of existing processes, the specification of the target framework, and its practical implementation within the SWE ServiceNetwork.The outcome of the activity shall enable the transition towards a new generation of the SWE Service Network and an updatedversion of the ESA SWE Service Portal.The procurement shall require the application of high standards in software engineering, theactive involvement of end-users within the R2O2R lifecycle, and the delivery of a professional, high-quality user experience for the web portal, including modern software practices, advanced graphical design, and robust human-machine interfaces.

title: RECEIVER TECHNIQUES AND ALGORITHMS FOR PNT SOLUTIONS WITH ONLY 1 AND 2 LEO SATELLITES IN VIEW - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view, based on the optimised fusion ofall the available estimations along time.Description: The use of LEO-based systems on top of current GNSS systems (in MEO orbits) is being considered to improve the achievable user performances, in particular in challenging user scenarios. To ensure that at least3 or 4 satellites are in view by any user on ground, a much larger number of LEO satellites than for MEO is required to be used inthis case. In this context, it is of high interest to investigate techniques exploiting signals received by LEO satellites when only 1 and 2 LEO satellites are in view by a ground user. This would enable, for example, to exploit LEO satellites with reduced constellations with a limited available number of satellites visible, and/or while a full LEO-PNT constellation is still being deployed. Theobjective of this activity is to design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view,, including transitions between 1 and 2 satellites, based on the optimised fusion of all the available estimations along time, including at least:- ToA (Time-of-Arrival), FoA (Frequency-of-Arrival) and AoA (Angle-of-Arrival)-like estimations; - Multi-epoch / synthetic apertureprocessing solutions exploiting the fast satellite geometry change; and, additionally, if introducing benefits to the above : - Clock coasting; - Inertial sensors measurements; - DEM (Digital Elevation Model)/height sensors ; The suitability of the proposed solutions is aimed to be assessed based both on simulations and real data. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define and design innovative techniques and algorithms in the areas identified above; - Develop the required tools/software for the assessment/test of the innovative techniques and algorithms; - Assess/test the different techniques and algorithms in realistic simulated conditions, and with real signals from LEO satellites; - Identify the most promising techniques/algorithms based on the results obtained;- Propose the way-forward to further mature each of the promising techniques/algorithms identified.Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses
